keyQuestions.text: Parity gaps and overbuild: against OpenBot's eight parts and the 002 synthesis, what does a small team still lack after all eleven phases, and what do the plans build that is not needed or duplicates another phase or the runtime?

Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and verbs each of the eleven plans names exist with the shapes it assumes, and are its test and verify commands runnable in this checkout?

Cross-phase consistency: do the eleven phases agree on the shared records (by: actor, grants, operators.json, conversation JSONL, memory files, state-root layout, HonoredPosture fields, bots --json output) and is the build order and dependency graph sound?

Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, restarts, lost or duplicated messages and answers, concurrent approvals from terminal and chat, prompt injection through memory, skills or chat, and routine until and fatigue edge cases.
Which planned surfaces duplicate the built runtime or another phase and can be cut for a small team, ranked by the build time they save?
Which runtime modules do more than one phase modify, and in what order must those phases land so the parser, record and index shapes do not collide?

keyFindings.text: **`operators.json` is a direct parent/child contradiction: the parent forbids any child from building it and phase 011 builds it.** The parent says "The rest of the small-team model (§12): two roles in one `operators.json` and a shared host at mode 0770. No child builds them; 001 lands the actor field alone" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:94`). Phase 001 repeats the deferral (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:100`) and phase 006 repeats it again (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:107`). Phase 011 then decides "yes, the minimal roster" and makes REQ-005 depend on it: "Only an actor named `owner` or listed in `members` in `operators.json`…" (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177`, `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281`). **Severity P0** — 011 cannot meet its own REQ-005 without a file the parent forbids, and no phase owns that file's schema, its write path or its mode. Fix: move `operators.json` ownership into phase 001 (it already owns `actor.ts` and the actor precedence), change `spec.md:94` to "001 lands the actor field and the `operators.json` roster; no other child builds it", and change `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:281` to read the roster from 001 instead of landing it.

**Phase 001's Definition of Ready contains a verify command that cannot pass as written.** It requires "`rg -n 'SCHEMA_VERSION' .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts` prints one line reading `'2'`" (`001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:39`), but the file holds three `SCHEMA_VERSION` occurrences — the declaration at line 55, the guard at line 253 and the insert at line 677 — so the command prints three lines and the check fails before any work starts. **Severity P2.** Fix: change the check to `rg -n "const SCHEMA_VERSION = " .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts` prints `55:const SCHEMA_VERSION = '2';`.

**Phase 011 builds five transports where the small-team model needs one plus the terminal, which is the largest overbuild in the packet.** The phase adds `channel.ts`, `channel-link.ts`, `channel-approval.ts`, `channel-queue.ts` and five transports — Telegram, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp and terminal — plus six verbs (`bots channel list|link|unlink|send|listen|drain`) (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:111-116`). The 002 small-team model says "the terminal is the client" and the skip list rules out mobile (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:103-116`). WhatsApp additionally needs a public HTTPS URL or tunnel and a Meta business account, which the phase itself lists as an operator prerequisite (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:116`). **Severity P1.** Fix: cut `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3 In Scope to Telegram long polling plus the terminal fallback, move Slack, Signal and WhatsApp into a new `012-messaging-transports` phase, and move `channel-approval.ts` and `channel-queue.ts` into the retained slice only if the Telegram path needs them.

**Phase 011 duplicates phase 006's approval surface with a second, parallel approval index.** 011 adds `channel-approval.ts`, "a file-backed `approval-v1:<item-id>:<index>` index and the numbered or YES/NO reply grammar, so a restart loses no prompt" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/spec.md:112`), while 006 already owns `grants` on the needs-you item and the precedence ladder at that gate (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:105-110`). Two indexes mean two answers can be recorded for one item, and the grant scope 006 writes is not what 011 reads. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3, replace the parallel index with "the channel reads the needs-you item id from the delivery entry and writes the answer through `bots answer --scope`, reusing 006's grant"; keep only a restart-safe `sent-prompt` marker, not an approval index.

**Phase 011-messaging-channels has no row in the 002 ranked build order, so it is net-new scope that the parity research never sized or ranked.** The 002 order has eleven items: activity/actor, routine layer, computer exposure, memory, grants, per-bot apps, vault, skills, conversations, TUI, desktop shell (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:139-158`). Items 1-9 map one-to-one onto phases 001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010; item 10 (TUI) is phase 003; item 11 (desktop) is explicitly out of scope (`specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:85`). Phase 011 answers none of them. **Severity P1.** Fix: add a twelfth row to the 002 ranked order (or a "post-parity" note in `specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md` §3) that names messaging channels, its size and its risk, and state in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §1 that the phase is post-parity scope rather than a research slice. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:139-158] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:114-143]

**The parent packet's own audit trail is stale: it says "ten phases" and its `bots.cjs` row omits phases 003 and 011.** `spec.md:100` reads "This table is the audit trail of the surfaces the ten phases touch", and `spec.md:104` lists `.skilled/bin/bots.cjs` as modified by "001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010" — but phase 003 adds the `ui` verb (`003-terminal-screen/spec.md:41`) and phase 011 adds six `channel` verbs (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:116`). **Severity P2.** Fix: change "ten phases" to "eleven phases" at `spec.md:100` and change the phase column at `spec.md:104` to "001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010, 011".

**The shared-host mode is deferred by every phase, so a two-person team cannot read the queue after all eleven phases.** The 002 model says "State folders are created mode 0700, so a shared root is unreadable by a second person. A group and mode 0770 is the whole change" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:104`), and the runtime pins `STATE_DIR_MODE = 0o700` (`state-root.ts:46`). The parent defers it (`spec.md:94`), 001 defers it (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:100`) and 006 defers it (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:107`). **Severity P1** if the team shares a host, P2 if every operator has their own account. Fix: add one requirement to `001-activity-and-actor/spec.md` §4 — "when `operators.json` lists more than one member, the state root is created 0770 with the operator group" — or state in `spec.md` §3 that a shared host is unsupported and why.

**The small-team authority check is a parity gap: after all eleven phases, `bots answer` still never checks who may answer.** The 002 model specifies "Two roles. An `owner` (who installed the jobs) and `member`, in one `operators.json` under the state root, checked by `bots answer` before it writes" (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:103`). Phase 001 defers the roster (`001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:100`), phase 006 defers it (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:107`), and phase 011 builds a roster only to gate channel senders (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177`). No phase adds the check to `answer.ts`. **Severity P1.** Fix: add one requirement to `006-approval-grants/spec.md` §4 — "`bots answer` refuses with `actor-not-permitted` when the resolved actor is neither `owner` nor in `members` of `operators.json`" — and one acceptance row for it.

**Correction to iteration 1 finding 5: 011's `channel-approval.ts` is a message-id-to-item-id index, not a second answer store, so the duplication is narrower than iteration 1 claimed — but it still duplicates a field the run record already carries.** Phase 011 states "The answer path, which records the answer and queues the resume, so a channel answer reuses it rather than writing an item" (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:49`), which is correct reuse. The index exists to map an inbound reply to an item after a restart (`:112`, `:209`). But `DeliveryEntry` already carries `itemId` for a parked question — `resolveDeliveryEntries` sets `entry.itemId = exit.needsYouItemId` when the run parked (`delivery.ts:143-146`) — so the only genuinely new datum is the outbound message id. **Severity P2** (downgraded from P1). Fix: in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3, replace the separate `approval-v1` index with "the delivery entry gains `sentMessageId`, and an inbound reply resolves through the run record's delivery entry"; keep the index only if a requirement needs a lookup the run record cannot serve.

**Five phases modify `definition.ts`, and no plan sequences them, so the parser branches collide at merge time.** Phase 002 adds `routine` (`002-routine-layer/plan.md:85`), 005 adds `memory` (`005-memory/spec.md:97`), 007 adds `apps` (`007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:100`), 008 resolves `secrets` (`008-vault/spec.md:97`) and 009 adds `skills` (`009-skills/spec.md:167`). Each adds a key to the same `ITEM_KEYS`-style allowlist and a validation branch in the same function. The parent's phase map orders them 002, 005, 007, 008, 009, which is serial, but no plan says the parser change is the merge point or names the allowlist it extends. **Severity P1.** Fix: add one row to `specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md` §3 under Phase Transition Rules — "`definition.ts`'s frontmatter allowlist is the shared merge point for phases 002, 005, 007, 008 and 009; each phase adds its key and its validation branch in the same commit as its parser test" — and name the allowlist in each of the five plans' AFFECTED SURFACES rows.

**Phase 003 adds a second toolchain and a new CI job to a Node repository, and no plan sequences that prerequisite.** The phase creates `crates/bots-tui/`, a Rust crate, and "a `bots-tui` CI job that runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`" (`003-terminal-screen/spec.md:41-45`). The repository has no `crates/` directory today, and the runtime's Definition of Done for every other phase is `npx vitest run` plus `npx tsc --noEmit`. **Severity P2.** Fix: add `cargo` and a Rust toolchain to `003-terminal-screen/plan.md` §2 Definition of Ready, and gate the `bots-tui` CI job behind a `paths: crates/**` filter so a Node-only change does not pay for a Rust build.

**Phase 008 lifts three rakazo files for policy the phase could state in a paragraph, adding a per-file third-party provenance obligation.** The phase says "Lift rakazo's `secret-matcher.ts`, `secrets-guard.ts` and `vault.ts` policy with Apache-2.0 notices and one `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry per lifted file" (`008-vault/spec.md:99`). All three files exist in the reference repo (`specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts`, `.../node/secrets-guard.ts`, `.../integrations/vault.ts`), so the lift is possible. But the store the phase actually builds is `security` plus a 0600 file (`008-vault/spec.md:97`), and the only behaviour it needs from the lift is the literal matcher. **Severity P2.** Fix: in `008-vault/spec.md` §3, keep `secret-matcher.ts` and drop `vault.ts` and `secrets-guard.ts` unless a requirement names a policy only they provide; if dropped, remove their `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` rows from the same section.

**Phase 009 adds three hard checker invariants for one optional field, in a checker that has eighteen hard and zero advisory invariants.** The checker's `HARD_INVARIANTS` list holds eighteen ids and `ADVISORY_INVARIANTS` is empty (`bot-check.cjs:39-65`). Phase 009 adds `skills-unknown`, `skills-too-large` and a third (`009-skills/spec.md:167`, `:130`). A byte cap is a size policy, not a correctness invariant, and the checker already has an advisory tier built for exactly this. **Severity P2.** Fix: in `009-skills/spec.md` §4, move `skills-too-large` to `ADVISORY_INVARIANTS` (WARN by default, FAIL under `--strict`) and keep `skills-unknown` hard; update REQ-007 and the acceptance rows to match.

**Phase 011's `channel-queue.ts` re-implements the file-queue primitive the runtime already ships, as a second queue with its own backoff table.** `request-queue.ts` is already "a file queue under the user-level state root … every state change of a request is one rename between sibling folders, so a request is in exactly one folder at a time and two consumers can never both claim it", with a seen-key marker that makes a re-sent event a duplicate and a `quarantine/` folder for a refused request (`request-queue.ts:1-25`). Phase 011 adds `channel-queue.ts` as "the durable send queue with enqueue-before-I/O, unknown-after-send and the 0/5/25/120/600 s backoff" (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:61`, `:113`, `:135`). The two queues solve the same problem in opposite directions, and the second one duplicates the rename-and-seen-key discipline without reusing it. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `011-messaging-channels/spec.md` §3, replace "Add `channel-queue.ts`" with "Extract the rename-and-seen-key primitive from `request-queue.ts` into `file-queue.ts` and build the outbound queue on it", and add one acceptance row that the inbound queue's existing tests still pass unchanged.

**Overbuild verdict, ranked by build time saved: phase 011 is the only phase whose scope can be cut by more than a third without losing a 002 item.** The ranked cuts: (1) 011 to Telegram plus terminal, dropping Slack, Signal and WhatsApp (iteration 1 finding 2); (2) 011's `channel-queue.ts` rebuilt on the `request-queue.ts` primitive (iteration 2 finding 1); (3) 011's `channel-approval.ts` replaced by `sentMessageId` on the delivery entry (iteration 2 finding 2); (4) 006's ladder cut to one rung (finding 1 above); (5) 008's two unnecessary lifts (iteration 2 finding 4); (6) 009's third hard invariant (iteration 2 finding 5); (7) 003's ungated Rust CI job (iteration 2 finding 3). Phases 001, 002, 004, 005 and 010 have no cuttable surface: each adds one record field or one file and reuses an existing primitive. **Severity P1 for cuts 1-4, P2 for 5-7.** Fix: apply cuts 1-4 to the phase specs before the build starts; they remove roughly one phase of work and no 002 item.

**Parity verdict: all eight 002 parts are covered by the eleven phases, and the gaps that remain are inside parts, not missing parts.** Conversations → 010 and 011; Routines → 002; Memory → 005; Skills → 009; Apps → 007; Computer → 004; Approvals → 006; Activity → 001; plus the terminal screen → 003 and the vault → 008 (`specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:21-95`, `specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/spec.md:114-143`). The gaps that survive all eleven phases, ranked: (a) who may approve — no phase adds the `operators.json` check to `bots answer` (iteration 1 finding 4); (b) app reach — the allowlist is advisory (finding 3 above); (c) a shared host — every phase defers the 0770 mode (iteration 1 finding 8); (d) per-action policy inside the executor — deferred by 002 and again by 006 (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:105`); (e) memory provenance beyond the needs-you confirmation — 005 records `type`, `date`, `actor` and `source` but no review state (`005-memory/spec.md:97`); (f) skill recording from a demonstration — deferred by 009 (`009-skills/spec.md:167`); (g) conversation streaming and attachments — deferred by 010. **Severity P1 for (a)-(c), P2 for (d)-(g).** Fix: add (a), (b) and (c) as requirements to phases 006, 007 and 001 respectively; record (d)-(g) in the parent `spec.md` §3 Out of Scope with the phase that defers each, so the packet states its own limits.

**Phase 006 builds a four-rung approval ladder in which three rungs can never fire, because no store supplies their inputs.** The phase says `approval-ladder.ts` "walks kinds, then rules, then auto-review, then extra vigilant, and lets the first rung that says ask decide" (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:96`), and then puts the inputs for rungs 2, 3 and 4 out of scope: "A rules store, an auto-review switch and an extra-vigilant switch — the ladder takes all three as inputs and no store supplies them yet" (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:103`). Only rung 1 (action kinds) can ever return `ask`, so three quarters of the ladder is unreachable code with its own tests. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `006-approval-grants/spec.md` §3, replace the four-rung ladder with "rung 1 (kinds) is built; rungs 2-4 are documented in `bots-run/references/approval-ladder.md` as the precedence order a later packet fills", and delete the three unreachable branches from REQ-002 and its acceptance rows.

**Phase 006's `--scope always` does not outlive the item it answers, so the scope name promises persistence the phase does not build.** The phase records the scope on the item and says "A saved rule that outlives its item — rung 2 has no store in this phase, so an `always` scope is recorded on the item and read by the resumed prompt, not by a later item" (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:104`). An operator who answers `always` will expect the next item of the same kind to be pre-approved, and it will not be. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `006-approval-grants/spec.md` §4, either rename the scope to `once|conversation|deny` and drop `always`, or add the rule store that makes `always` mean what it says; the rename is the smaller change and matches the phase's own Out of Scope.

**Phase 007's `apps:` allowlist is not an allowlist: the child's own MCP config pins `UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` and overrides the inherited value, which the phase admits.** The phase sets `UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` in the child environment to the run's filtered config (`007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:100`), then puts the override out of scope: "`.claude/mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, `opencode.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json` each set `UTCP_CONFIG_FILE` to `.utcp_config.json` explicitly, and an explicit value in an MCP server block overrides the inherited one … this phase records what the runner wrote and honored rather than claiming the child is confined" (`007-per-bot-apps/spec.md:104`). A bot that declares `apps: []` can still reach every server in the repository config. **Severity P1.** Fix: in `007-per-bot-apps/spec.md` §3, either remove the four pins and update `.skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/mcp-doctor-lib.sh:291` in the same phase, or rename the key to `appsAdvisory`, state in `bots-author/references/bot-definition.md` that it is a record and not a boundary, and drop the `apps-unknown-server` hard invariant to advisory because it cannot enforce reach.

**Phase 003's Definition of Ready is circular: it requires a successful build of the crate the phase creates.** The DoR says "`cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/bots-tui/Cargo.toml` exits 0 on the empty crate" (`003-terminal-screen/plan.md:41`), but `crates/` does not exist in this checkout, so the command fails before the phase starts and passes only after the phase has done the work the DoR is meant to gate. **Severity P2.** Fix: move the build check to the Definition of Done and keep only `cargo --version` in the DoR; `cargo 1.92.0` is installed here, so that half already passes.

**Phase 004's Definition of Done can never pass in build order: it requires `SCHEMA_VERSION = '2'` after phase 001 has bumped it to `'3'`.** Phase 004's DoD says "`rg -n \"SCHEMA_VERSION = '2'\" .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/status-index.ts` prints one line" (`004-computer-exposure/plan.md:49`), and its AFFECTED SURFACES verification repeats the same command (`004-computer-exposure/plan.md:82`). Phase 001's AFFECTED SURFACES says the same file "gains the `actor` column and a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump" and its verification expects `'3'` (`001-activity-and-actor/plan.md:76`), and the parent phase map makes 004 depend on 001 (`spec.md:124`). The runtime is at `'2'` today (`status-index.ts:55`), so 004's check passes only before 001 lands and fails after. **Severity P0** — the phase cannot be marked done, and a builder who trusts the DoD will either revert 001's bump or ship a failing gate. Fix: change both occurrences in `004-computer-exposure/plan.md` (lines 49 and 82) to `SCHEMA_VERSION = '3'`, and add one sentence to 004's §3 saying the index is already at `'3'` when this phase starts.

**Six phases edit `.skilled/bin/bots.cjs` without updating its `.opencode/bin/bots.cjs` mirror, so the mirror drifts and the three phases that gate on `diff -q` fail.** The two files are byte-identical today (`diff -q` exits 0) and the mirror is a regular file, not a symlink. Phases 003, 010 and 011 list the mirror in AFFECTED SURFACES and require `diff -q .skilled/bin/bots.cjs .opencode/bin/bots.cjs` to print nothing (`003-terminal-screen/plan.md:49`, `010-conversations/plan.md:50`, `011-messaging-channels/plan.md:52`). Phases 001, 002, 005, 006, 008 and 009 edit `.skilled/bin/bots.cjs` and never mention the mirror, so after 001 lands the two files differ and 003's DoD fails. **Severity P1.** Fix: add the `.opencode/bin/bots.cjs` row to the AFFECTED SURFACES table of phases 001, 002, 005, 006, 008 and 009, or add one Phase Transition Rule to `spec.md` §3 — "every phase that edits `.skilled/bin/bots.cjs` updates `.opencode/bin/bots.cjs` in the same commit and proves it with `diff -q`".

**Three phases assume a two-word verb grammar the CLI does not have, and only one of them names the parser change.** `VERB_SPECS` is a flat map of single-word verbs with an `ids` count — `run`, `disable`, `enable`, `pause`, `resume`, `inbox`, `enqueue`, `drain`, `answer`, `schedule`, `status` (`bots.cjs:63-77`) — and `parseArgs` takes the first positional as the verb, so `bots skill propose <run-id>` parses as verb `skill` with id `propose`, `bots secret set demo` as verb `secret` with id `set`, and `bots channel list` as verb `channel` with id `list`. Phase 008 names the problem and the fix: "`VERB_SPECS` is the closed verb list | update: the `secret` verb group" (`008-vault/plan.md:91`). Phase 009 says only "`skill` is not in `VERB_SPECS`, so the CLI exits 2" (`009-skills/spec.md:91`) and phase 011 says only "`bots channel list` prints `bots: unknown verb: channel`" (`011-messaging-channels/plan.md:40`); neither names the grammar change. **Severity P1.** Fix: add one row to `008-vault/plan.md` §3 defining a `VERB_GROUPS` table (verb → sub-verb → ids/options) and the `parseArgs` change that reads it, then have `009-skills/plan.md` and `011-messaging-channels/plan.md` cite that row instead of assuming the grammar exists.

**Three plans have no runnable Definition of Ready, so a builder cannot tell whether the pre-state holds.** Phases 002, 007 and 009 use only generic `[x]` items — "Problem statement clear and scope documented", "Success criteria measurable", "Dependencies identified" (`002-routine-layer/plan.md:39-42`, `007-per-bot-apps/plan.md:39-41`, `009-skills/plan.md:39-42`) — while the other eight name a measured command and its expected output. **Severity P2.** Fix: give each a measured pre-state, matching the pattern the other eight use: 002 `rg -n 'routine' .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/definition.ts` exits 1; 007 `rg -n 'apps' .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/definition.ts` exits 1; 009 `rg -n 'skills' .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/definition.ts` exits 1.

**A channel approval records no grant scope, so the same item answered from the terminal and from chat produces two different records.** Phase 006 adds `grants` to the needs-you item with "the scope the answer granted" and `bots answer --scope once|conversation|always|deny` (`006-approval-grants/spec.md:94-99`). Phase 011 puts "Phase 006's `grants` field and ladder" out of scope (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:53`) and its approval requirement checks only the actor against `operators.json` (`011-messaging-channels/spec.md:177`). An operator who answers from chat therefore records no scope, and the resumed run's prompt names no granted scope. **Severity P1.** Fix: delete the Out of Scope line at `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:53` and add a requirement that a channel answer passes `--scope` through `bots answer`, defaulting to `once` when the reply grammar carries no scope word.

**Five phases modify `state-root.ts`, a second merge hotspot beside `definition.ts`.** Phases 002, 005, 008, 010 and 011 each add a folder or a path helper to the same module (`002-routine-layer/spec.md:129`, `005-memory/spec.md:113`, `008-vault/spec.md:119`, `010-conversations/spec.md:115`, `011-messaging-channels/spec.md:141`). The parent's phase map orders them serially, but no plan names the module as a shared merge point. **Severity P2.** Fix: extend the Phase Transition Rule proposed in iteration 2 finding 6 to name both `definition.ts` and `state-root.ts` as shared merge points, and add the `state-root.ts` row to each of the five plans' AFFECTED SURFACES tables.
